A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the subcutaneous injection of 15 units of diphtheria toxin antitoxin in a small area of the irradiated skin of rabbits up to 7 days after the exposure was more effective in neutralization of a large dose of toxin than in the corresponding area of nonirradiated rabbits.

the results indicated that a sublethal dose of X irradiation, 1000 r in this case, was followed by an increased susceptibility of the irradiated area to the toxic effects of a homologous toxin and a decreased susceptibility to the protective effects of antitoxins.

we have shown that X irradiation in small doses of the order of 1000 r does not alter the antitoxic activity of the antitoxic protein of the diphtheria serum, but that the protein is retained in the injected area for a much longer time than it is retained in non-irradiate areas.
